territorial_scope.description: Applies to social network service providers carrying on their activity in France, under new LCEN Art. 6-7 I.

evidence.quote: exerçant leur activité en France [carrying on their activity in France]

summary.short: Amends France's Law for Trust in the Digital Economy (LCEN): social network providers must refuse under-15 accounts without parental authorization, use age checks meeting an ARCOM framework, and display harassment-prevention messages. Entry into force is set by decree, no later than three months after EU Commission's response on notification.
summary.long: The law amends France's LCEN (Law No. 2004-575) in five respects. Art. 1 defines online social network services. Art. 2 extends the illegal-content categories hosts must address (harassment, threats, privacy, security and listed Penal Code offences). Art. 3 requires social networks to show harassment-prevention messages. Art. 4 inserts Art. 6-7: providers operating in France must refuse accounts for under-15s without parental authorization, obtain authorization for existing under-15 accounts, inform users and parents of risks, enable parental suspension and time-use controls, and verify age using technical solutions meeting an ARCOM framework. ARCOM may issue a formal notice (15 days to respond) and ask the Paris court president to order compliance; breach carries a fine up to 1% of prior-year worldwide turnover. Non-profit encyclopedias and educational or scientific directories are exempt. Art. 5 adds 10-day response deadlines (8 hours in emergencies) to LCEN Art. 6 VI. Art. 6 requires a government report on youth and platforms within one year. Art. 7 sets entry into force by decree within three months after the EU Commission's response to notification; some Art. 6-7 provisions apply later (one and two years).

entities.name: Commission européenne
entities.function: Its response that the law is compliant with EU law (after notification) is the condition for the entry-into-force decree (art. 7 I).

evidence.quote: la réponse de la Commission européenne permettant de considérer le dispositif législatif lui ayant été notifié comme conforme au droit de l'Union européenne

notes: Entry into force is set by decree no later than three months after the EU Commission response (art. 7 I), so the document gives no fixed date. Art. 7 II staggers two provisions: the second sentence of art. 6-7 I first paragraph starts two years later, and art. 6-7 II starts one year later. Art. 4 I requires technical solutions conforming to an Arcom referential, while art. 4 II refers to a 'solution technique certifiée'; the terms differ and are not reconciled in the text. Art. 4 IV defers implementing rules to a Conseil d'État decree, which is not part of this document. Art. 4 III excludes non-profit online encyclopedias and non-profit educational or scientific directories.
